newsitem.title: UK: Rushie slams paper for printing ex-wife's comments.
newsitem.headline: Rushie slams paper for printing ex-wife's comments.

text.p: Author Salman Rushdie criticised a British newspaper on Friday for printing derogatory statements by his former wife, who left him months after he drew an Iranian death sentence in 1989.

In a letter to The Guardian, Rushdie said he wanted to set the record straight after his ex-wife Marianne Wiggins described him as self-obssessed and accused him of failing to support other authors whose lives were threatened because of their work.

"As I have not seen or spoken to Ms Wiggins for nearly seven years, and as her own heroism ran out (and so did she) just four months after the fatwa (death ruling), she can scarcely be thought an expert wintess," he wrote.
The Indian-born author said he had devoted "a significant proportion of my time and thought to the defence of other persecuted writers.
"For many years I have been president of the International Parliament of Writers, whose chief reason for existence is to help writers in trouble," he said.
He added that he had also chaired rallies, spoken at events and fought and written about the persecution of writers in countries such as Algeria, Turkey, Nigera and Bangladesh.
The fatwa on Rushdie was issued in 1989 by Iran's spiritual leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomenei because of alleged blasphemy against Islam in his novel "Satanic Verses".
Rushdie was driven into hiding and has been under constant police protection. International attempts to get the fatwa lifted have failed.
American-born author Wiggins, who was contacted by The Guardian after being declared bankrupt in Britain over an unpaid tax bill, divorced Rushdie in 1993 after five years of marriage.
"To repeat Ms Wiggins's unfounded slanders while pretending to be unaware of the truth is, sir, to join her in her defamations," Rushdie wrote.
As for Wiggins, he said he was sorry to hear she was declared bankrupt just a few years after she received a substantial six-figure divorce settlement.
